h: The Trumpets Unite Yisrael and Overcome the Strife of Midyan

p: In Midrash Tanchuma on this parsha:
and likewise Roshei Chodashim and Festivals,
and when they went to war against Midyan,
with trumpets they took vengeance, etc."
(at the beginning of this parsha and in Parshas Beha'alosecha):
"Since it says, 'And they shall sound, etc.,'
might whatever comes first in the verse
it specified in one of them
that the princes come before the congregation."
Now this needs to be understood:
in the passage of the trumpets,
did it put the congregation before the princes?
וְכֵן בִּתְחִלַּת הַפָּרָשָׁה כְּתִיב (בְּמִדְבַּר י, ב)
And likewise at the start of the passage it is written (Bamidbar 10:2):
and they shall be for you for summoning the congregation, etc.,"
and the princes are not mentioned at all.
But the function of the trumpets
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כו, ב)
as is written in Rashi's commentary (Rosh Hashanah 26b):
that the mitzvah of the day is with trumpets,
and every assembly is with trumpets, etc."
as one man with one heart.
And this was through the trumpets.
the main thing is that they all be
in which there are none of the sinners of Yisrael
And this is what Rashi said,
that they all be one assembly
And this is the meaning of
"and they shall be for you for summoning the congregation":
as one man with one heart.
אֶל פֶּתַח אוֹהֶל מוֹעֵד (בְּמִדְבַּר י, ג)
at the entrance of the Ohel Mo'ed" (Bamidbar 10:3)
as it was at the Giving of the Torah,
"as one man with one heart, etc.";
and this was the preparation for the Giving of the Torah.
the main thing is that Yisrael be
the verse made them all comrades";
that they be as one man with one heart,
in the words of the verse,
which is the aspect of the moon,
then is the time to repair even the galbanum,
which alludes to the sinners of Yisrael,
to give off a good fragrance
therefore it too is sanctified with trumpets.
And likewise on Shabbasos, at the Musaf offerings,
"'And on the day of your rejoicing' (Bamidbar 10:10)
there too the mitzvah is with trumpets.
For the Musaf of Shabbos is counted
as corresponding to "the Tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
as is written in the holy Zohar
as one man with one heart.
בִּבְחִינַת וְעַמֵּךְ כּוּלָּם צַדִּיקִים (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ ס, כא)
in the aspect of "And your people are all righteous" (Yeshayahu 60:21),
And this is the portion of Moshe Rabbeinu,
that at the Giving of the Torah
he instilled in the heart of all Yisrael
to be as one man with one heart,
וַיֵּרֶד ה׳ עַל הַר סִינַי (שְׁמוֹת יט, כ)
And this is what is said:
and they said (Tanchuma Beha'alosecha 10, and elsewhere):
and no one else uses them";
that is, this power was given to Moshe,
"and they shall be for you for summoning the congregation"
that he would effect this in their hearts,
that they all be as one man.
the main thing is that Yisrael be
as one man with one heart,
and that even the sinners of Yisrael be repaired
when they are in one bond,
which gives off a good fragrance
with the ten spices of the incense.
they prevail over the nations of the world;
כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם מַה לְקַטְרֵג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
when they have something with which to accuse Yisrael
And this is what is said:
"and they shall be for you for summoning the congregation"
for the main function of the trumpets
that they all be as one man;
and therefore the princes are not mentioned at all.
in the order of the signals of the blasts,
the blast with both of them,
the princes shall gather to you" (Bamidbar 10:4).
that they be as one man with one heart.
שֶׁהוּא הָיָה נָשִׂיא עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
for he was prince over all Yisrael
to be as one man with one heart.
And this is what the Sifrei says,
And this is what the Tanchuma cited above says:
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good";
regarding everything that is the opposite of good;
for then, at the addition to Shabbos,
in the eyes of Hashem Yisbarach,
that from everything there will be "very good."
which is the peace of the upper and the lower ones,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת קֹרַח)
as is written in the holy Zohar (beginning of Parshas Korach),
is sanctified at the addition to Shabbos
as one man with one heart.
that in the war against Midyan,
בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן (שְׁמוֹת ב, טז)
on what is written, "the priest of Midyan" (Shemos 2:16)
it was necessary to conquer them
for this is the holiness of Yosef,
the death of Moshe Rabbeinu on this,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And this is what the Midrash Tanchuma cited above says:
"And when they went to war against Midyan,
with trumpets they took vengeance, etc.";
for the essence of the vengeance was
as one man with one heart,
the opposite of the kelipah of Midyan (strife).
for having caused them to sin,
that at the root, in truth,
and only they were the ones who troubled their souls.
